title: 2007 HMMT February General Round 1 Problem 5
statement: Find the smallest positive integer that is twice a perfect square and three times a perfect cube.

solutions.text: 648. Let \(n\) be such a number. If \(n\) is divisible by 2 and 3 exactly \(e_{2}\) and \(e_{3}\) times, then \(e_{2}\) is odd and a multiple of three, and \(e_{3}\) is even and one more than a multiple of three. The smallest possible exponents are \(n_{2}=3\) and \(n_{3}=4\). The answer is then \(2^{3} \cdot 3^{4}=648\).
